leading_positions.synthesis: Four members prefer B007 with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov under a discovery-centred citation (physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, enabling incretin therapy). They share the view that the prize should reward the discovery rather than the product, and that Holst and Drucker are fixed. They differ in how firmly they hold Mojsov: El Manira and Wahren-Herlenius describe the third name as a judgement call, and Linnarsson and Perlmann say they would move only if the record showed her priority to be weaker than credited. All four acknowledge that Habener is not on the supplied list and that Knudsen's omission is the main criticism.

Two members, Sandberg and the chair, prefer B007 with Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, under a citation naming both the physiology and the development of long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists. They share Holst and Drucker with the first group and differ only on the third name: they argue that acylation-based half-life extension is what turned the physiology into a medicine. Neither claims the Mojsov priority question is settled against her. Sandberg says he would accept the Mojsov trio if the committee wants a purely discovery-level prize. The chair has said he would move if the committee judges peptide identification to be more decisive.

areas_of_agreement: All six members' round-1 configurations are a single B007 part, and all six rank it first on science and maturity: a complete arc from proglucagon processing and GLP-1 receptor biology to replicated outcome-trial benefit in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease.
Holst and Drucker are named by all six members in their B007 configurations.
No member raises a maturity concern about B007, and each states that the three-person cap, not the merit, is the problem.
All six list B041 and B004 as their two alternatives, in different orders (B004 first for El Manira and Perlmann, B041 first for the other four). No member lists any other ballot as an alternative.
Members see B004 (Walter and Mori) as having the cleanest two-person attribution on the shortlist, and see B041 (CAR-T) as having the stronger clinical record. No member contests either point.
Habener's absence from the supplied B007 credit, and Eshhar's absence from the B041 credit, are acknowledged as limits on what any citation can safely claim.
scientific_disputes: Whether the basic-discovery contribution (identification and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) or the long-acting analogue design (acylation, albumin binding, once-daily and once-weekly dosing) is the more decisive step. Members disagree on whether Knudsen's work is a discovery-level contribution (Sandberg, Svenningsson) or a development step (El Manira, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius).

Whether the prize should be anchored in physiology, as the four-member group proposes, or should name the development of therapies, as the two-member group proposes. Sandberg and Linnarsson each say the outcome depends on this principle.

How to rank B004 against B041 as the first alternative. Four members place B041 first, citing durable remissions, while El Manira and Perlmann place B004 first, citing cleaner attribution and mechanism. Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson accept that B004's clinical consequence is still emerging.
Linnarsson ranks B002 (TOR) above B004 on breadth but regards its clinical reach as narrower than its basic importance. Svenningsson and others question whether B002 has a clean second or third name.
attribution_disputes: B007 third name: Mojsov (El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius) versus Knudsen (Sandberg, Svenningsson). Members state that Mojsov's priority for the active form is disputed in the literature and that they cannot verify it from the supplied record.

Whether leaving Mojsov out would settle a contested priority question against her without evidence (Wahren-Herlenius, Perlmann), or whether including her rests on a claim no one has verified (Svenningsson).

B041: whether June and Sadelain alone is a defensible pair (Linnarsson, and El Manira agrees), or whether Rosenberg's adoptive-transfer work is foundational (Wahren-Herlenius). Sandberg notes that dropping Rosenberg does not resolve the Eshhar originator question.
B004: the supplied credit lists Walter and Mori only; Wahren-Herlenius notes that Ron and Kaufman are not credited, so the clean two-person attribution depends on the list as supplied.

Several statements describe other members' opening rankings (for example of B017, B001 and B041) differently from how those members describe their own positions. Only the explicit round-1 configurations and alternatives are counted here.
maturity_disputes: No member disputes the maturity of B007.

B004: the mechanism is secure after about three decades, but its disease and therapeutic consequences are described as indirect or still developing (El Manira, Perlmann, Wahren-Herlenius, Linnarsson).
B041: Linnarsson regards toxicity and the lack of solid-tumour efficacy as limits on the size of the impact, not on whether the discovery is real. Maturity is not otherwise disputed.
Long-term safety and durability of incretin therapy in obesity is flagged as still accruing by several members, none of whom says this changes the ranking.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Svenningsson (chair) disclosed a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and co-authorship with Perlmann on dopamine-neuron topics. Perlmann also discloses co-authored works with Svenningsson. Neither involves a shortlisted candidate, and neither reports a need for recusal.

El Manira disclosed a 2009 paper with Perlmann and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, and uses optogenetics (B032) as a research tool. He did not place B032 in his configuration or alternatives. Perlmann confirms one co-authored work with El Manira.

Linnarsson disclosed co-authorship with Sandberg (eight works, not independently audited) and the 2016 Science spatial-transcriptomics paper. Sandberg disclosed co-authorship with Linnarsson and Frisén and a postdoc with Christopher Burge. Neither involves a credited name.
Sandberg noted that his field is close to B008 (antisense correction of SMN2 splicing) and did not choose it for his configuration or alternatives.
Perlmann disclosed nuclear-receptor co-authorship with Ronald Evans. Evans is not credited on any shortlisted ballot.
Wahren-Herlenius disclosed a Bergen affiliation and co-authors Kuchroo and Sonesson, none of whom is credited. No member reports a conflict requiring recusal.
questions_for_round2: Should the B007 citation be anchored in the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, which supports Mojsov, or should it name the development of long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonists, which supports Knudsen? What principle should decide, and can the committee state it before choosing the name?

What evidence in the supplied record bears on Mojsov's priority for identifying and synthesising the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide relative to Habener and others? Is that evidence strong enough to include or exclude her?

Can any three-person B007 configuration be worded so that it does not read as a ruling on the contested priority or as a prize for a commercial product? Specifically, would Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, or Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, be better supported by its citation text?

If B007 stalls on credit, which alternative do members move to first, B004 or B041? What would each need to resolve: B004's indirect clinical consequence, or B041's Eshhar originator question and the Rosenberg inclusion?

Is a two-part prize pairing B007 with B004 or B041 feasible within the three-person limit, given that B007 alone needs three names and B004 would leave B007 with only Drucker and Holst? If it is not, should round 2 treat the prize as a single B007 part?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete agreement on the ballot (B007 alone) and on the first two names, and a four-to-two split on the third name that tracks a stated difference over whether the prize rewards discovery or development. Both groups say they would move on that principle, so round 2 can resolve it by deciding the principle first. The record counts only the six explicit configurations and alternatives, and the chair's own position is in the minority-of-two group.
